@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+# The explicit weighted Bessel kernel
+
+## Abstract
+
+A two-mode counterexample to weighted Bessel-kernel positivity.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Successive positive zeros).**
+
+$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{j}\left(0\right) = 0\\\operatorname{j}\left(1\right) = \operatorname{firstZero}\left(0\right)\\\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), \operatorname{j}\left(n + 2\right) = \operatorname{sInf}\left(\{x: \mathbb{R} | (0 < x) \land ((\operatorname{j}\left(n + 1\right) < x) \land (\operatorname{nbessel}\left(0, x\right) = 0))\}\right)\end{aligned}$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Analytic/BesselRedheffer/AcostaBabbKernelRefutation.j` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ryan L. Acosta Babb (2024). *A partial converse to the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma for Bessel–Fourier series of order zero*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2410.17681](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2410.17681). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17681v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Lemma 2.2, p. 6: “Let jₘ denote the mth positive zero of J₀. Then”. The real function nbessel 0 is J₀. The sequence is indexed from one, with an unused value zero at index zero; the first zero is firstZero 0, and later entries are infima of the positive zeros strictly above the preceding entry. Only the first two entries are needed below; their infima are attained and lie in the rational intervals described below.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The printed partial sum).**
+
+$$\forall (\alpha: \mathbb{R}), \forall (m: \mathbb{N}), \forall (x: \mathbb{R}), \operatorname{S}\left(\alpha, m, x\right) = \sum_{k \in \operatorname{Finset.Icc}\left(1, m\right)} (\operatorname{j}\left(m\right)^{\alpha} \cdot \operatorname{nbessel}\left(0, \operatorname{j}\left(k\right) \cdot x\right))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Analytic/BesselRedheffer/AcostaBabbKernelRefutation.S` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ryan L. Acosta Babb (2024). *A partial converse to the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma for Bessel–Fourier series of order zero*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2410.17681](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2410.17681). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17681v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Section 3, p. 7: “Let us write $S^{\alpha}_{m}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{m} j_{m}^{\alpha} J_{0}(j_{k} x)$.” The factor is jₘ raised to alpha even inside the sum over k. Consequently this printed S does not give the printed Cesaro equality for the explicit weighted kernel; S is retained separately.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The explicit weighted kernel).**
+
+$$\forall (\alpha: \mathbb{R}), \forall (M: \mathbb{N}), \forall (x: \mathbb{R}), \operatorname{K}\left(\alpha, M, x\right) = if (M = 0) then 1 else \sum_{m \in \operatorname{Finset.Icc}\left(1, M\right)} ((1 - \frac{(m: \mathbb{R})}{(M: \mathbb{R}) + 1}) \cdot \operatorname{j}\left(m\right)^{\alpha} \cdot \operatorname{nbessel}\left(0, \operatorname{j}\left(m\right) \cdot x\right))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Analytic/BesselRedheffer/AcostaBabbKernelRefutation.K` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ryan L. Acosta Babb (2024). *A partial converse to the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma for Bessel–Fourier series of order zero*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2410.17681](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2410.17681). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17681v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Section 3, p. 7, the explicit right-hand display is “$= \sum_{m=1}^{M} (1 - \frac{m}{M + 1}) j_{m}^{\alpha} J_{0}(j_{m} x)$.” The separate sentence is “We will also set $K^{\alpha}_{0}(x) \equiv 1$ when $M = 0$.” Here the sum ranges over positive natural indices, and both m and M are cast to real numbers in the weight. K uses this explicit formula, independently of the preceding printed S equality.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Conjecture 1).**
+
+$$claim = (\forall (\alpha: \mathbb{R}), (0 \le \alpha) \Rightarrow ((\alpha \le \frac{1}{2}) \Rightarrow (\forall (M: \mathbb{N}), \forall (x: \mathbb{R}), (0 \le x) \Rightarrow ((x \le 1) \Rightarrow (0 \le \operatorname{K}\left(\alpha, M, x\right))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Analytic/BesselRedheffer/AcostaBabbKernelRefutation.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ryan L. Acosta Babb (2024). *A partial converse to the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma for Bessel–Fourier series of order zero*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2410.17681](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2410.17681). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17681v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Conjecture 1, p. 10: “For all, $0 \leq \alpha \leq \frac{1}{2}$, $M \in \mathbb{N}$ and $x \in [0,1]$, $K^{\alpha}_{M}(x) \geq 0$.” The natural M includes zero; alpha and x are real numbers, and both intervals are closed. K is the explicit weighted formula on p. 7.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (Refutation at two modes).**
+
+$$\neg (\forall (\alpha: \mathbb{R}), (0 \le \alpha) \Rightarrow ((\alpha \le \frac{1}{2}) \Rightarrow (\forall (M: \mathbb{N}), \forall (x: \mathbb{R}), (0 \le x) \Rightarrow ((x \le 1) \Rightarrow (0 \le \operatorname{K}\left(\alpha, M, x\right))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/BesselRedheffer/AcostaBabbKernelRefutation.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/ab2410` (refuted) by `D5/S3/Analytic/BesselRedheffer/AcostaBabbKernelRefutation.result`.
+

+

+# Nonnegative exponential transforms
+
+## Abstract
+
+A positive measure supported on the nonnegative real axis has a singularity at a finite boundary of exponential integrability.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Holomorphic extension and exponential integrability).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/NonnegativeBoundary.integrable_exp_of_holomorphic_extension`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/NonnegativeBoundary.integrable_exp_of_holomorphic_extension` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let mu be a measure on the real line supported on the nonnegative axis. Suppose t lies in the interior of the interval where exp(t*x) is integrable. Let F be holomorphic on the complex ball of radius r about t and agree near t with the exponential transform integral exp(z*x) dmu(x). For every h with 0<=h<r, exp((t+h)*x) is integrable. The Taylor coefficients at t are the moments integral x^n*exp(t*x) dmu(x) divided by n factorial. These moments are nonnegative. Taylor convergence at t+h and the monotone interchange of the nonnegative exponential series with integration give the asserted integrability.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Continuation along the real ray).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/NonnegativeBoundary.integrable_exp_on_real_ray`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/NonnegativeBoundary.integrable_exp_on_real_ray` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let mu be a measure supported on the nonnegative real axis and suppose its exponential integral converges at some real parameter. Let U be open and contain every real t<a, and let F be holomorphic on U. Suppose F agrees locally with the defining transform at every t<a in the interior of the interval of exponential integrability. Then exp(t*x) is integrable for every t<a. If one such parameter failed, positivity makes the convergence interval downward closed with finite supremum c<a. A ball about c contained in U and the preceding Taylor argument give integrability strictly to the right of c, a contradiction.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (A singularity at the convergence boundary).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/NonnegativeBoundary.nonnegative_exponential_boundary`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/NonnegativeBoundary.nonnegative_exponential_boundary` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David Vernon Widder (1941). *The Laplace Transform*. DOI: [10.1515/9781400876457](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400876457).
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let mu be a measure on the nonnegative real axis and c a finite real number. Assume exp(t*x) is integrable for every t<c and is not integrable for any t>c. There is no positive radius r and holomorphic F on the ball about c of radius r which agrees with the exponential transform on the part of that ball with Re(z)<c. Indeed choose t=c-r/4. Taylor convergence on the ball about t of radius r/2 implies integrability at t+r/3>c, contradicting the convergence boundary. Replacing z by -s gives the corresponding nonnegative Laplace-transform theorem at its finite abscissa of convergence. This formulation uses a general positive measure, extending Widder's nonnegative locally integrable function formulation.
+

+# Positive Laplace transforms and zeta poles
+
+## Abstract
+
+Positivity bounds the zeta residues of a continued Laplace transform.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Convergence throughout the regular real ray).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/PositiveLaplacePoleObstruction.laplace_integrable`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/PositiveLaplacePoleObstruction.laplace_integrable` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let mu be a positive measure supported on nonnegative reals, with Laplace integral L(s) converging for every real part greater than B. Let x0>1 and let R be holomorphic for Re(s)>a. Suppose in the initial overlap L(s)=e*P(s)+R(s)+k*x0^(-s)/s, where P(s) is minus one half the logarithmic derivative of (z-1)*zeta(z), evaluated at z=s+1/2. Then the defining integral converges for every real sigma>max(a,0). Multiplication by s times the normalized zeta factor propagates the initial identity on the connected convergence domain. The normalized factor has no positive real zeros. The nonnegative Laplace boundary theorem therefore excludes a convergence boundary on the available real ray.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Exclusion of a positive translated zero).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/PositiveLaplacePoleObstruction.no_positive_pole`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/PositiveLaplacePoleObstruction.no_positive_pole` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Under the preceding hypotheses, assume |e|=1. Every nontrivial zeta zero rho satisfies Re(rho)-1/2<=max(a,0). Otherwise its translated pole lies in the interior of actual Laplace convergence. The actual transform is analytic there, whereas its continued expression has nonzero residue -e*m/2 for the positive zero multiplicity m. Multiplication by the distance from the pole gives incompatible limits.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The one-half budget at an imaginary-axis pole).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/PositiveLaplacePoleObstruction.critical_pole_budget`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/PositiveLaplacePoleObstruction.critical_pole_budget` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Under the same hypotheses, assume a<0, |e|=1, and let rho be a nontrivial zero with Re(rho)=1/2. Then k>=1/2. For sigma tending to zero from above, sigma*L(sigma) tends to k, while sigma*L(sigma+i*Im(rho)) tends to -e*m/2. The triangle inequality for the same positive integral bounds the modulus of the second expression by the first real expression. Taking limits gives m/2<=k, and m>=1 proves the assertion.
+

+# The normalized zeta logarithmic derivative
+
+## Abstract
+
+Removing the pole of zeta at one before taking its logarithmic derivative gives a principal term regular on the nonnegative real axis. The translated nontrivial zeros have negative half-integer residues.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (The normalized zeta factor has no positive real zero).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.normalized_zeta_ne_zero_real`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.normalized_zeta_ne_zero_real` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The entire completion Z(s) of (s-1)zeta(s) is nonzero at every positive real s. Away from one this follows from the sign of real zeta; at one its value is one.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Cancellation of the density pole).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.regularizedPrincipal_eq`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.regularizedPrincipal_eq` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let Z(s) be the entire completion of (s-1)zeta(s). At a point s different from one half where zeta(s+1/2) is nonzero, the quantity -Z'(s+1/2)/(2Z(s+1/2)) equals -zeta'(s+1/2)/(2zeta(s+1/2))-1/(2(s-1/2)).
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Regularity along the nonnegative real axis).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.regularizedPrincipal_analyticAt_real`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.regularizedPrincipal_analyticAt_real` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every nonnegative real sigma, the cancelled principal term is complex analytic near sigma. Zeta has no real zero between zero and one, has no zero to the right of one, and Z(1)=1. These facts include regularity at sigma=0 and sigma=1/2.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Isolation of translated nontrivial zeros).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.normalized_zeta_eventually_ne_zero`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.normalized_zeta_eventually_ne_zero` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a nontrivial zeta zero rho, the function Z(s+1/2) is nonzero in a punctured neighborhood of rho-1/2. The local factorization into a positive integer power times an analytic nonvanishing function gives the isolation.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (Multiplicity determines the translated residue).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.regularizedPrincipal_zero_residue`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Zeta/ZetaLogDerivativeRegularity.regularizedPrincipal_zero_residue` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every nontrivial zeta zero rho there is a positive integer m such that (s-(rho-1/2)) times the cancelled principal term tends to -m/2 as s approaches rho-1/2 through distinct points. The analytic-unit factorization of zeta supplies m; the subtracted density term is regular at this translated zero.
+

+# The compact adjoint of the forward price kernel
+
+## Abstract
+
+The literal Mellin adjoint retains the complete signed arithmetic response of the original forward kernel.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Compact support at every evaluation point).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Adjoint.adjointKernel_eq_compact`

+The Mellin adjoint q_s(t) is the integral over x>=x0 of x^(-s-1)*k(x,t). For each t it equals the compact integral over x in [x0,max(x0,t)]. Centers x>=t have zero kernel value.

+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Adjoint.adjointKernel_center_integrable`

+# Analytic dependence of the inverse-coordinate remainder
+
+## Abstract
+
+The actual inverse-coordinate forward remainder and its differentiated Chebyshev tail depend holomorphically on the Mellin parameter.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Integrating an entire family with compact uniform bounds).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Analytic.entire_integral_of_compact_bound`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Analytic.entire_integral_of_compact_bound` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+On a finite measure space, let f(s,a) be almost everywhere strongly measurable in a for every s, and entire in s for almost every a. Assume that every compact parameter set K has a finite constant C such that |f(s,a)|<=C for all s in K outside one null set. Then integral f(s,a) da is entire. Countable difference quotients give measurability of the parameter derivative. Cauchy's estimate on unit circles inside a ball of radius two bounds that derivative by an integrable constant, allowing differentiation under the integral.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Entire dependence of the actual remainder).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Analytic.adjointRemainder_entire`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Analytic.adjointRemainder_entire` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For each fixed t>8, the actual remainder r(t,s)=t^(-s-1/2)*(N(t,s)-1/2) is entire in s. Here N is the fixed triangular integral of the normalized inverse-coordinate kernel. Its parameter dependence is an exponential of (-s-1/2)*log(x(t,z)/t), multiplied by the original weight ratio and inverse Jacobian. The proved kernel bounds are uniform on each compact parameter set, so the finite-measure integral theorem applies.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The time derivative is also entire in the parameter).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Analytic.adjointRemainder_timeDerivative_entire`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Analytic.adjointRemainder_timeDerivative_entire` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For each fixed t>8, the time derivative of r(t,s) is entire in s. The exact derivative-under-integral formula for N differentiates the same triangular kernel. Its integrand is a finite sum of polynomials in s times the original exponential, with real coefficients depending on the inverse coordinate. The uniform time-derivative estimate gives compact parameter bounds. This proves entire dependence before forming the Chebyshev tail.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Holomorphy of the actual differentiated remainder tail).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Analytic.adjointRemainder_tail_holomorphic`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Analytic.adjointRemainder_tail_holomorphic` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Assume alpha>=0 and there are real C and t0 such that |psi(t)-t|<=C*t^alpha for every t>=t0. For every fixed x0>8, integral_(x0,infinity) (psi(t)-t)*partial_t r(t,s) dt is holomorphic for Re(s)>alpha-7/10. The actual compact C1 remainder bound gives |partial_t r(t,s)|<=A_K*t^(-Re(s)-17/10) on each compact K. Derivatives as functions of t are measurable; countable parameter difference quotients provide the remaining measurability. The Chebyshev remainder integral theorem then applies with these proved properties of the actual kernel.
+

+# The forward adjoint remainder
+
+## Abstract
+
+The inverse-coordinate forward adjoint has an exact triangular main coefficient and a uniform C1 remainder.
+
+Use x(t,z) determined by t=x+z*x^(4/5), J(t,z)=1/(1+(4/5)*z*x(t,z)^(-1/5)), A(x,u)=w(x+u*x^(4/5))/w(x), and P(t,z,s)=exp((-s-1/2)*log(x(t,z)/t)). The normalized coefficient is the integral of P*A*J on the fixed triangle 0<=z<=u<=1. The area of that triangle is exactly 1/2.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Correlated control of the integrand and its derivative).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Asymptotic.normalizedBody_C1_estimate`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Asymptotic.normalizedBody_C1_estimate` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For t>=8 and z,u in [0,1], the coefficient P*A*J is differentiable in t. With p=-s-1/2 and C(s)=(2*|p|+50)*exp(2*|p|)+10, its difference from one has norm at most C(s)*t^(-1/5), and its time derivative has norm at most C(s)*t^(-6/5). The derivative of the ratio A uses the same moving center in numerator and denominator.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (The exact inverse-coordinate integral).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Asymptotic.inverseAdjoint_eq_iterated`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Asymptotic.inverseAdjoint_eq_iterated` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The inverse-coordinate adjoint is t^(-s-1/2) times the normalized triangular coefficient. Fubini and the identity t^(-s-1/2)*P=x(t,z)^(-s-1/2) identify it with the integral over 0<=z<=1 of x(t,z)^(-s-1/2)*integral_z^1 A(x(t,z),u) du divided by 1+(4/5)*z*x(t,z)^(-1/5).
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Uniform C1 control after subtracting the principal term).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Asymptotic.inverseAdjoint_uniform_C1_remainder`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Asymptotic.inverseAdjoint_uniform_C1_remainder` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let r_s(t)=t^(-s-1/2)*(normalizedAdjoint(t,s)-1/2). For every compact K in the complex plane there is C_K>0 such that, for s in K and t>8, |r_s(t)|<=C_K*t^(-Re(s)-1/2)*t^(-1/5) and |d_t r_s(t)|<=C_K*t^(-Re(s)-3/2)*t^(-1/5).
+
+The derivative passes under an integral on a fixed compact triangle. Both the normalized coefficient and its derivative have uniform bounds there. The product rule is applied only after subtracting the exact coefficient 1/2. Local boundedness of the explicit parameter constants then gives the compact uniform estimates.
+

+# Finite Mellin corrections
+
+## Abstract
+
+Bounded intervals of the original adjoint contribute entire Mellin corrections.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (An integrable density on positive compact centers).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/FiniteMellin.compact_mellin_entire`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/FiniteMellin.compact_mellin_entire` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+If a>0 and f is complex-valued and integrable on [a,b], then the integral of f(x)*x^(-s-1) over that interval is entire in s. Extend f by zero outside [a,b]. This integrable extension vanishes near zero and at infinity, so Mathlib's mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow applies at every complex parameter. Composing with negation gives the stated exponent.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Entire dependence at a fixed adjoint point).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/FiniteMellin.adjointKernel_entire`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/FiniteMellin.adjointKernel_entire` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For x0>=4 and every real t, the actual adjoint q_s(t) is entire in s. Its center integral has compact support in [x0,max(x0,t)], so the compact Mellin theorem applies to the original price kernel.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (A bounded interval of adjoint points).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/FiniteMellin.adjointKernel_finite_integral_entire`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/FiniteMellin.adjointKernel_finite_integral_entire` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For 4<=x0<=b, the integral of q_s(t) over [1,b] is entire. All its center integrals lie in [x0,b]. The original kernel lies between zero and one, and the Mellin powers are uniformly bounded on compact parameter sets. These bounds allow integration of the entire parameter family.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (The bounded signed correction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/FiniteMellin.finiteCorrection_entire`

+# The complete forward Mellin adjoint
+
+## Abstract
+
+Absolute Fubini retains every complete-prime-power contribution in the forward Mellin adjoint.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Absolute transport of the complete signed response).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Fubini.unbounded_forward_adjoint`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Fubini.unbounded_forward_adjoint` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let x0>=4 and let f be a measurable complex center weight. Assume that norm(f(x))*abs(T(x)) and norm(f(x))*V(x) are integrable over x>=x0, where V(x)=integral k(x,t) dt is the original continuous kernel mass. Then the literal adjoint integral of f(x)*k(x,t) is integrable in t, and its Lambda-weighted positive-integer values form an absolutely summable series.
+
+The integral of f(x)*T(x) equals that series minus the integral of the adjoint in t. Nonnegativity of the original kernel bounds its complete arithmetic row mass by abs(T(x))+V(x). This proves both product-integrability statements before either use of Fubini. Every prime power keeps its full log-prime weight.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Signed adjoint truncations recover the Mellin integral).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Fubini.forwardMellin_adjoint_tendsto`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Fubini.forwardMellin_adjoint_tendsto` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Assume alpha>=0 and an eventual power bound abs(psi(t)-t)<=C*t^alpha for all t>=t0. For x0>=4 and Re(s)>max(1/2,alpha-3/10), the actual adjoint q_s(t) is integrable over t>1. The difference between the sum of Lambda(n)*q_s(n) for 0<=n<=floor(b) and the integral of q_s(t) from 1 to b tends to the original forward Mellin integral as b tends to infinity.

+# Inverse coordinates for the original Mellin adjoint
+
+## Abstract
+
+The original forward Mellin adjoint admits an exact inverse-coordinate representation.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Exact change of variables in the Mellin adjoint).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/InverseTransport.adjointKernel_inverse_coordinates`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/InverseTransport.adjointKernel_inverse_coordinates` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For x0>=4 and t>=max(8,B(x0)), let x(t,z) be the positive solution of t=x+z*x^(4/5), and let D=1+(4/5)*z*x^(-1/5). Then the actual adjoint q_s(t), defined by integrating x^(-s-1)*k(x,t) over x>=x0, equals the integral over z in [0,1] of x(t,z)^(-s-1/2)*integral(w(x+u*x^(4/5))/w(x),u=z..1)/D.
+
+The original support reduces the center integral to [x(t,1),t]. The exact derivative x_z=-x^(4/5)/D gives the change of variables. Integrating the price derivative w=-lambda' on the same window produces the inner weight ratio; x^(8/5)/x^(11/10)=sqrt(x) then gives the principal Mellin exponent.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Identification with the normalized triangular adjoint).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/InverseTransport.adjointKernel_eq_inverseAdjoint`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/InverseTransport.adjointKernel_eq_inverseAdjoint` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For x0>=4 and t>=max(8,B(x0)), the actual Mellin adjoint equals the normalized triangular adjoint used for the uniform remainder estimates. The equality follows from the exact inverse-coordinate integral and Fubini on the fixed triangle.

+# One-half gaps for the complete forward response
+
+## Abstract
+
+Positive logarithmic transforms give one-sided oscillation bounds for the complete forward response.
+
+The response T is the complete real-center forward response with window H=x^(4/5). Theta is the supremum of Re(rho) over zeros in the open critical strip. The only unproved analytic number-theory input is the explicitly stated Theta error estimate. The positive logarithmic budget measure is the pushforward under y=log(x) of the nonnegative density (e*T(x)+k)/x on x>x0. Nonnegative Laplace-transform boundary singularities and the exact zeta residues supply the oscillation constraints.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Nonnegative logarithmic support).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.budgetMeasure_nonnegative`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.budgetMeasure_nonnegative` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For x0>=1, the pushforward by the real logarithm of the measure with density (e*T(x)+k)/x on x>x0 is supported on nonnegative real numbers. The density is read through its nonnegative part.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (An initial convergence half-plane).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.budget_exponential_integrable`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.budget_exponential_integrable` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let alpha>=0 and assume |psi(t)-t|<=C*t^alpha eventually. Suppose x0>=3 and e*T(x)+k>=0 for x>=x0. The positive logarithmic budget measure has a finite exponential integral at every Laplace parameter sigma>max(0,alpha-3/10).
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The exact positive budget transform).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.budget_transform`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.budget_transform` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Under the same hypotheses, the complex moment-generating function of the budget measure at -s equals e*F(s)+k*x0^(-s)/s for Re(s)>max(0,alpha-3/10). Here F is the Mellin integral of the complete forward response. The logarithmic pushforward and the density x^(-1) retain the exact Mellin Jacobian.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (A right-hand zero forces negative divergence).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.forward_response_unbounded_below_of_right_zero`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.forward_response_unbounded_below_of_right_zero` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let Theta be the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeta zeros. Assume that for every epsilon>0 there is C with |psi(t)-t|<=C*t^(Theta+epsilon) for t>=2. If some nontrivial zero has real part greater than one half, then for all real L and X there exists x>=X with T(x)<L. A zero can be selected with beta>max(1/2,Theta-1/5); a sufficiently small positive epsilon places its shifted pole strictly inside the positive-transform convergence region.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (The unconditional one-half lower obstruction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.forward_response_lower_kappa_gap`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.forward_response_lower_kappa_gap` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Under the displayed Theta error estimate, for every kappa<1/2 and every real X there exists x>=X with T(x)<-kappa. In the RH case, any nontrivial zero lies on the critical line and its Mellin residue has absolute value at least one half. Positivity bounds this residue by the assumed eventual lower budget. Outside RH the stronger negative-divergence theorem applies.
+
+**Theorem 1.6 (The one-half upper obstruction under RH).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.forward_response_upper_kappa_gap_of_rh`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.forward_response_upper_kappa_gap_of_rh` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Under RH and the Theta error estimate, for every K<1/2 and every real X there exists x>=X with T(x)>K. Apply the nonnegative transform to K-T(x); its critical-line residue has the opposite sign and the same absolute value.
+
+**Theorem 1.7 (Failure of RH forces positive divergence).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.forward_response_unbounded_above_of_not_rh`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/KappaGap.forward_response_unbounded_above_of_not_rh` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Under the Theta error estimate, failure of RH implies that for all real L and X there exists x>=X with T(x)>L. The functional equation supplies a zero to the right of the critical line. The transform of L-T has a nonzero shifted pole strictly inside its convergence region, which contradicts holomorphy there.

+# The continuous kernel mass
+
+## Abstract
+
+The continuous kernel mass.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Extending an eventual power bound).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/MellinConvergence.error_power_bound`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/MellinConvergence.error_power_bound` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let alpha>=0. If |psi(t)-t|<=C*t^alpha for every t>=t0, there is D>=0 such that |psi(t)-t|<=D*t^alpha for every t>=2. On the compact initial interval use monotonicity and nonnegativity of psi; outside it use the given estimate.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Power growth of the complete response).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/MellinConvergence.forwardResponse_power_bound`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/MellinConvergence.forwardResponse_power_bound` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let E(t)=psi(t)-t, H(x)=x^(4/5), and T(x)=sqrt(x)/H(x)^2 times the integral from 0 to H(x) of (E(x+u)-E(x))*w(x+u)/w(x). +# The generalized Mellin identity
+
+## Abstract
+
+The generalized Mellin identity.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (The generalized Mellin identity).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/MellinResidue.forward_kernel_mellin_residue`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/MellinResidue.forward_kernel_mellin_residue` (`✓ std3`). ∎

+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let alpha>=0 and assume there are real C and t0 with |psi(t)-t|<=C*t^alpha for every t>=t0. For each x0>=3, the Mellin integral F(s) of the original complete forward response has a remainder R holomorphic on Re(s)>alpha-7/10. +Write H(x)=x^(4/5). For t>0 and z>=0, x(t,z) is the unique positive solution of t=x+z*H(x). A globally increasing extension x+z*H(max(x,0)) defines the inverse without changing this positive solution.

+## Abstract

+# Transport of the original forward kernel
+
+## Abstract
+
+The original complete Chebyshev response has an exact finite signed price-kernel representation.
+
+Write E(t)=psi(t)-t, H(x)=x^(4/5), B(x)=x+H(x), lambda(t)=1/(t*log(t)), and w(t)=(log(t)+1)/(t^2*log(t)^2). The functions H, B, lambda, w, and E are the existing width, endpoint, g, weight, and discrepancy functions. The response is T(x)=sqrt(x)/H(x)^2 times the integral from 0 to H(x) of (E(x+u)-E(x))*w(x+u)/w(x).
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Existence of the finite response integral).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Transport.forwardResponse_intervalIntegrable`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Transport.forwardResponse_intervalIntegrable` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every x>1 the integrand defining T(x) is interval integrable. Monotonicity makes psi integrable on compact intervals; subtracting the continuous coordinate and multiplying by the continuous weight preserves this property.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (The complete finite signed price identity).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Transport.forwardResponse_eq_signed_price`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/Transport.forwardResponse_eq_signed_price` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every x>1, T(x)=sqrt(x)/(w(x)*H(x)^2) times the sum of Lambda(n)*(lambda(n)-lambda(B(x))) over x<n<=B(x), minus the integral from x to B(x) of lambda(t)-lambda(B(x)). The arithmetic sum is written as the difference of two right-closed weighted prefixes. Thus an initial atom is excluded, and a terminal atom has zero price difference. Every prime power carries the full von Mangoldt weight.
+
+The finite arithmetic integration-by-parts identity and its continuous counterpart are applied to the same price curve. Subtracting them produces E(t)-E(x). Translation t=x+u and the exact normalization give the stated original response.

+
+## Abstract
+
+The original forward weight ratio has quantitative value and derivative bounds.
+
+Use the existing functions H(x)=x^(4/5) and w(x)=(1+log(x))/(x^2*log(x)^2). For x>=4 and 0<=u<=1, let A(x,u)=w(x+u*H(x))/w(x). The center in the denominator moves together with the center in the numerator.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Value of the original ratio).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/WeightControl.weightRatio_sub_one`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/WeightControl.weightRatio_sub_one` (`✓ std3`). ∎

+
+The exact monotonicity and lower power bound for w give |A(x,u)-1|<=4*x^(-1/5). The lower bound uses (x/(x+u*H(x)))^4 rather than replacing the weight by a different window.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Cancellation in the correlated derivative).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/WeightControl.weightRatio_control`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ForwardKernel/WeightControl.weightRatio_control` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The ratio satisfies 0<=A(x,u)<=1. Put L(x)=(-2+1/(1+log(x))-2/log(x))/x, the logarithmic derivative of w. The derivative of A in x equals A(x,u)*(L(x+u*H(x))*(1+(4/5)*u*x^(-1/5))-L(x)). Its absolute value is at most 12*x^(-6/5).

+For x>=4, |L(x)|<=5/x and |L'(x)|<=8/x^2. The mean value theorem bounds L at the two correlated arguments. Their separation is u*H(x), so the difference has size at most 8*u*x^(-6/5). +# An identity-only residue set in Kohen's Conjecture 1
+
+## Abstract
+
+The unrestricted generalized central trinomial residue generation conjecture fails at p=3, a=3, b=1.
+
+Nadav Kohen, Density and Symmetry in the Generalized Motzkin Numbers mod p, arXiv:2411.03681v2, Conjecture 1, asks whether the first p generalized central trinomial coefficients generate the multiplicative group of the prime field whenever none is divisible by p. The conjecture quantifies over all integer parameters a and b. Its defining constant term is taken in the integer Laurent polynomial ring. The source is https://arxiv.org/html/2411.03681v2.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The defining Laurent polynomial).**
+
+$$\forall a \in \mathbb{Z},\; \forall b \in \mathbb{Z},\; step\left(a, b\right) = LaurentPolynomial.C\left(a\right) \cdot LaurentPolynomial.T\left(-1\right) + LaurentPolynomial.C\left(b\right) + LaurentPolynomial.C\left(a\right) \cdot LaurentPolynomial.T\left(1\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/ArithUnits/KohenMotzkinGenerationRefutation.step` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The integer parameters a and b give the Laurent polynomial aX^(-1)+b+aX. LaurentPolynomial.C includes an integer as a constant, while LaurentPolynomial.T takes an integer exponent, so the negative exponent is literal. No restriction on either parameter is imposed.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Integer constant terms).**
+
+$$\forall a \in \mathbb{Z},\; \forall b \in \mathbb{Z},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; central\left(a, b, n\right) = coeff\left(step\left(a, b\right)^{n}, 0\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/ArithUnits/KohenMotzkinGenerationRefutation.central` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural index n, central(a,b,n) is the coefficient of exponent zero in step(a,b)^n. This is the source's generalized central trinomial coefficient, computed as an integer before taking any residue. The generalized Motzkin coefficients are a different sequence and are not substituted here.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The first p residues in the unit group).**
+
+$$\forall p \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall a \in \mathbb{Z},\; \forall b \in \mathbb{Z},\; \forall u \in Units\left(ZMod\left(p\right)\right),\; u \in generators\left(p, a, b\right) \Leftrightarrow \left(\exists n \in \mathbb{N},\; n < p \land (u : ZMod\left(p\right)) = (central\left(a, b, n\right) : ZMod\left(p\right))\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/ArithUnits/KohenMotzkinGenerationRefutation.generators` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A unit u belongs to generators(p,a,b) exactly when its underlying residue is central(a,b,n) modulo p for some natural n<p. The indices 0 through p-1 are the canonical representatives of the source's indices in the prime field. Under the nondivisibility premise every such residue is nonzero and hence a unit. This set therefore retains all the source generators.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (The complete unrestricted generation assertion).**
+
+$$claim \Leftrightarrow \left(\forall p \in \mathbb{N},\; Nat.Prime\left(p\right) \Rightarrow \left(\forall a \in \mathbb{Z},\; \forall b \in \mathbb{Z},\; \left(\forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; n < p \Rightarrow \left(\neg ((p : \mathbb{Z}) \mid central\left(a, b, n\right))\right)\right) \Rightarrow Subgroup.closure\left(generators\left(p, a, b\right)\right) = \operatorname{top}\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/ArithUnits/KohenMotzkinGenerationRefutation.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural prime p and every pair of integers a,b, assume that p divides none of central(a,b,n) for 0<=n<p. The conclusion says that the subgroup generated by their residues is the whole multiplicative unit group of ZMod p. Subgroup.closure includes the identity, inverses and arbitrary finite products. The premise adds no condition that p does not divide a or b. This is the generating assertion of Conjecture 1; the subsequent statements introduced as equivalent or consequent in the source do not replace it.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (The assertion is false).**
+
+$$\neg claim$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/ArithUnits/KohenMotzkinGenerationRefutation.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Specialize the universal assertion to p=3, a=3 and b=1. Extracting the constant terms of the zeroth, first and second powers gives 1, 1 and 1+2*3^2=19. These are all the indices less than three, and none of the three integers is divisible by three. Their residues are all one. Thus every generator belongs to the identity subgroup, and the least-subgroup property of Subgroup.closure places the whole generated subgroup there. The residue two is an actual unit modulo three and differs from one. It belongs to the whole unit group but cannot belong to the generated subgroup, contradicting the asserted equality. The coefficient extraction uses distributivity and exact integer arithmetic; the subgroup obstruction uses the group closure law. The proof refutes the unrestricted assertion. A variant imposing that p does not divide a is a different assertion and is not settled here.
+

+# Sun's absolute-difference permanent congruences
+
+## Abstract
+
+Both absolute-difference permanent congruences in Sun Conjecture 4.2(i).
+
+**Definition 1.1 (A).**
+
+$$\forall p \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall s \in \mathbb{Z},\; \forall j \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(p\right),\; \forall k \in \operatorname{Fin}\left(p\right),\; \operatorname{A}\left(p, s, j, k\right) = \lvert (\operatorname{val}\left(j\right):\mathbb{Z}) + 1 - \left((\operatorname{val}\left(k\right):\mathbb{Z}) + 1\right) + s\rvert $$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Permanental/SunAbsoluteDifferenceCongruences.A` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Zhi-Wei Sun (2022). *Arithmetic properties of some permanents*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2108.07723](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2108.07723). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.07723v7>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The matrices in (4.3) and (4.4), p. 25, are “per[|j − k|]” and “per[|j − k + 1|]”, with 1 ⩽ j,k ⩽ p. The integer shift s unifies their entries. Source indices are val(j)+1 and val(k)+1; each value is cast to ℤ before subtraction and absolute value.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (claim).**
+
+$$claim = (\forall p \in \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{Nat.Prime}\left(p\right) \Rightarrow \left(\operatorname{Odd}\left(p\right) \Rightarrow \left(((p:\mathbb{Z}) \mid (2 \cdot \operatorname{Matrix.permanent}\left(\operatorname{A}\left(p, 0\right)\right) + 1)) \land ((p:\mathbb{Z}) \mid (2 \cdot \operatorname{Matrix.permanent}\left(\operatorname{A}\left(p, 1\right)\right) - 1))\right)\right))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Permanental/SunAbsoluteDifferenceCongruences.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Zhi-Wei Sun (2022). *Arithmetic properties of some permanents*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2108.07723](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2108.07723). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.07723v7>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Conjecture 4.2(i), p. 25: “(i) For any odd prime p, we have per[|j − k|]₁⩽ⱼ,ₖ⩽ₚ ≡ −½ (mod p) and per[|j − k + 1|]₁⩽ⱼ,ₖ⩽ₚ ≡ ½ (mod p).” The displays are (4.3) and (4.4), respectively.
+
+Nat.Prime and Odd express exactly an odd prime. Matrix.permanent uses the sum of column-indexed permutation products, equal to the source's row-indexed sum by inversion of the permutation. Since 2 is invertible modulo an odd prime, the two integer divisibilities are precisely (4.3) and (4.4). The same p serves both conjuncts.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (result).**
+
+$$\forall p \in \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{Nat.Prime}\left(p\right) \Rightarrow \left(\operatorname{Odd}\left(p\right) \Rightarrow \left(((p:\mathbb{Z}) \mid (2 \cdot \operatorname{Matrix.permanent}\left(\operatorname{A}\left(p, 0\right)\right) + 1)) \land ((p:\mathbb{Z}) \mid (2 \cdot \operatorname{Matrix.permanent}\left(\operatorname{A}\left(p, 1\right)\right) - 1))\right)\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Permanental/SunAbsoluteDifferenceCongruences.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/sun210842` (proved) by `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Permanental/SunAbsoluteDifferenceCongruences.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"sun210842","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Combinatorics/Permanental/SunAbsoluteDifferenceCongruences.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Zhi-Wei Sun (2022). *Arithmetic properties of some permanents*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2108.07723](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2108.07723). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.07723v7>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Alternating row and column signs give circulants without changing their permanents. A prime-order fixed-point count on the permutation-weight fibers leaves only translations in characteristic p. Fermat's identity and a telescoping alternating sum then evaluate both permanents. The prime circulant ingredient is the Brualdi–Newman congruence; the two absolute-difference reductions yield the stated divisibilities.

+# The simple evolution algebra automorphism maximum
+
+## Abstract
+
+The full automorphism maximum for simple complex evolution algebras.
+
+A complex evolution algebra has a finite natural basis with zero mixed products. Its multiplication need not be associative or unital. The full automorphism group consists of all complex linear equivalences preserving multiplication on every pair of vectors.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Simplicity).**
+
+$$\forall (A : \operatorname{Type}), ([\operatorname{AddCommGroup}\left(A\right)] [\operatorname{Module}\left(\mathbb{C}, A\right)] \forall (mu : \operatorname{LinearMap}\left(\mathbb{C}, A, \operatorname{LinearMap}\left(\mathbb{C}, A, A\right)\right)), (\operatorname{IsSimple}\left(mu\right) = ((\operatorname{productSpan}\left(mu\right) \ne \operatorname{Bot}.\operatorname{bot}) \land (\forall (J : \operatorname{Submodule}\left(\mathbb{C}, A\right)), ((\forall (x : A), ((x \in J) \Rightarrow (\forall (y : A), ((mu\left(x, y\right) \in J) \land (mu\left(y, x\right) \in J))))) \Rightarrow ((J = (\operatorname{Bot}.\operatorname{bot})) \lor (J = (\operatorname{Top}.\operatorname{top}))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/QuadraticForms/EvolutionAlgebras/SimpleEvolutionAutomorphismMaximum.IsSimple` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Yolanda Cabrera Casado; Mercedes Siles Molina; M. Victoria Velasco (2016). *Evolution algebras of arbitrary dimension and their decompositions*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.01832v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The survey's Theorem 6 uses simplicity in the usual ideal sense. Its cited Cabrera Casado, Siles Molina and Velasco source, arXiv:1601.01832v2, section 4, page 18, states: “We recall that an algebra A is simple if A² ≠ 0 and 0 is the only proper ideal.” Here A² is productSpan, and ideals are all complex vector subspaces absorbing products on both sides. They are not restricted to spans of natural-basis vectors.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Conjecture 4).**
+
+$$\operatorname{claim} = (\forall (n : \mathbb{N}), ((1 \le n) \Rightarrow ((\forall (A : \operatorname{Type}), ([\operatorname{AddCommGroup}\left(A\right)] [\operatorname{Module}\left(\mathbb{C}, A\right)] [\operatorname{FiniteDimensional}\left(\mathbb{C}, A\right)] \forall (I : \operatorname{Type}), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(I\right)] \forall (mu : \operatorname{LinearMap}\left(\mathbb{C}, A, \operatorname{LinearMap}\left(\mathbb{C}, A, A\right)\right)), (\forall (b : \operatorname{Module}.\operatorname{Basis}\left(I, \mathbb{C}, A\right)), ((\operatorname{Module}.\operatorname{finrank}\left(\mathbb{C}, A\right) = (n)) \Rightarrow ((\forall (i : I), (\forall (j : I), ((i \ne j) \Rightarrow (mu\left(b\left(i\right), b\left(j\right)\right) = (0))))) \Rightarrow ((\forall (x : A), (\forall (y : A), (mu\left(x, y\right) = (mu\left(y, x\right))))) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{IsSimple}\left(mu\right)) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{Finite}\left(\operatorname{Aut}\left(mu\right)\right)) \land (\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{card}\left(\operatorname{Aut}\left(mu\right)\right) \le \operatorname{max}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{factorial}\left(n\right), n \cdot (2^{n} - 1)\right))))))))))) \land (\exists (mu : \operatorname{Product}\left(n\right)), ((\operatorname{Module}.\operatorname{finrank}\left(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Coord}\left(n\right)\right) = (n)) \land ((\operatorname{commutative}\left(mu\right)) \land ((\operatorname{hasNaturalBasis}\left(mu\right)) \land ((\operatorname{IsSimple}\left(mu\right)) \land ((\operatorname{Finite}\left(\operatorname{Aut}\left(mu\right)\right)) \land (\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{card}\left(\operatorname{Aut}\left(mu\right)\right) = (\operatorname{max}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{factorial}\left(n\right), n \cdot (2^{n} - 1)\right))))))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/QuadraticForms/EvolutionAlgebras/SimpleEvolutionAutomorphismMaximum.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ivan Kaygorodov; Cándido Martín González; Antonio Viruel (2026). *Evolution algebras: a survey of results and a list of open problems*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.22248](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.22248). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22248v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Conjecture 4, section 2.3, page 28: “Over ℂ, the maximal order of the automorphism group of a simple n-dimensional evolution algebra is max{n!, n(2ⁿ−1)}.” The dimension n is positive. The universal part ranges over arbitrary complex vector spaces A, finite index types I, bilinear products mu and natural bases b, with finrank equal to n. The existential part gives a product on Coord n attaining the bound. Finite is stated before Nat.card, so an infinite group cannot meet the bound by having natural cardinality zero.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The attained maximum).**
+
+$$\forall (n : \mathbb{N}), ((1 \le n) \Rightarrow ((\forall (A : \operatorname{Type}), ([\operatorname{AddCommGroup}\left(A\right)] [\operatorname{Module}\left(\mathbb{C}, A\right)] [\operatorname{FiniteDimensional}\left(\mathbb{C}, A\right)] \forall (I : \operatorname{Type}), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(I\right)] \forall (mu : \operatorname{LinearMap}\left(\mathbb{C}, A, \operatorname{LinearMap}\left(\mathbb{C}, A, A\right)\right)), (\forall (b : \operatorname{Module}.\operatorname{Basis}\left(I, \mathbb{C}, A\right)), ((\operatorname{Module}.\operatorname{finrank}\left(\mathbb{C}, A\right) = (n)) \Rightarrow ((\forall (i : I), (\forall (j : I), ((i \ne j) \Rightarrow (mu\left(b\left(i\right), b\left(j\right)\right) = (0))))) \Rightarrow ((\forall (x : A), (\forall (y : A), (mu\left(x, y\right) = (mu\left(y, x\right))))) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{IsSimple}\left(mu\right)) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{Finite}\left(\operatorname{Aut}\left(mu\right)\right)) \land (\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{card}\left(\operatorname{Aut}\left(mu\right)\right) \le \operatorname{max}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{factorial}\left(n\right), n \cdot (2^{n} - 1)\right))))))))))) \land (\exists (mu : \operatorname{Product}\left(n\right)), ((\operatorname{Module}.\operatorname{finrank}\left(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Coord}\left(n\right)\right) = (n)) \land ((\operatorname{commutative}\left(mu\right)) \land ((\operatorname{hasNaturalBasis}\left(mu\right)) \land ((\operatorname{IsSimple}\left(mu\right)) \land ((\operatorname{Finite}\left(\operatorname{Aut}\left(mu\right)\right)) \land (\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{card}\left(\operatorname{Aut}\left(mu\right)\right) = (\operatorname{max}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{factorial}\left(n\right), n \cdot (2^{n} - 1)\right)))))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/QuadraticForms/EvolutionAlgebras/SimpleEvolutionAutomorphismMaximum.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/kmvc4-simpleaut` (proved) by `D5/S3/QuadraticForms/EvolutionAlgebras/SimpleEvolutionAutomorphismMaximum.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"kmvc4-simpleaut","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/QuadraticForms/EvolutionAlgebras/SimpleEvolutionAutomorphismMaximum.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Ivan Kaygorodov; Cándido Martín González; Antonio Viruel (2026). *Evolution algebras: a survey of results and a list of open problems*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2610.22248](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.22248). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22248v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Simplicity forces the support graph to be strongly connected. Every support path projects to an orbit of the successor permutation on the least successor-compatible quotient, so this permutation has a single orbit. Invertibility of the structure map supplies a permutation supported on the arrows. Restricting it to consecutive quotient fibers gives bijections, forcing every fiber to have the same positive size k. If the quotient has h elements, then n=hk.
+
+The joint bound for the actual algebra group becomes h(2ʰ−1)(k!)ʰ. For h,k at least two, an induction using ascending factorials bounds this by (hk)!. The cases h=1 and k=1 give n! and n(2ⁿ−1), respectively. The argument uses the actual kernel and permutation image of the same algebra.
+
+The cyclic product has full group order n(2ⁿ−1). The product with structure matrix I+J, where every entry of J is one, is simple and has full group order n!: every permutation lifts, while loops force every diagonal automorphism to be the identity. Choosing the larger family proves attainment in every positive dimension, including dimension one. The upper-bound argument also works without a separate commutativity hypothesis when the mixed products of a finite natural basis vanish.
+

+# Exact semimonotone order does not imply invertibility
+
+## Abstract
+
+A four-dimensional singular matrix has exact semimonotone order three, so exact semimonotone order does not force a negative determinant or an inverse.
+
+Source: Bharat Pratap Chauhan and Dipti Dubey, On semimonotone matrices of exact order two, arXiv:2603.00639v1, Section 2, Definition 3.1 and Remark 4.1, second unlettered bullet. The binding version is available at https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00639v1. The question reads: “Is it true that if A belongs to E_{0_k}, then det A < 0 and A inverse exists and is a Z-matrix?” Its introductory range is n at least three and one at most k less than n. The first bullet concerning negative-entry counts is a separate question.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Semimonotone).**
+
+$$(\operatorname{Semimonotone}\left(A\right)) \Leftrightarrow (\forall (x: \iota \to \mathbb{R}), ((x \ne 0) \Rightarrow ((\forall (i: \iota), (0 \le \operatorname{x}\left(i\right))) \Rightarrow (\exists (i: \iota), ((0 < \operatorname{x}\left(i\right)) \land (0 \le \operatorname{mulVec}\left(A, x\right)_{i}))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/QuadraticForms/SemimonotoneExactOrderInverseRefutation.Semimonotone` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bharat Pratap Chauhan; Dipti Dubey (2026). *On semimonotone matrices of exact order two*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00639>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an arbitrary finite index type iota and a real square matrix A, every nonzero entrywise nonnegative real vector must have a strictly positive coordinate whose image coordinate is nonnegative. Zero coordinates are allowed. This is the ordinary E_0 predicate from Section 2, rather than strict semimonotonicity or the source's almost-class condition.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (IsExactOrder).**
+
+$$(\operatorname{IsExactOrder}\left(n, k, A\right)) \Leftrightarrow ((k \le n) \land ((\forall (\alpha: \operatorname{Finset}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right)), ((\operatorname{card}\left(\alpha\right) = n - k) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{Semimonotone}\left(A_{\alpha\alpha}\right)))) \land (\forall (\alpha: \operatorname{Finset}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right)), ((n - k < \operatorname{card}\left(\alpha\right)) \Rightarrow (\neg \operatorname{Semimonotone}\left(A_{\alpha\alpha}\right))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/QuadraticForms/SemimonotoneExactOrderInverseRefutation.IsExactOrder` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bharat Pratap Chauhan; Dipti Dubey (2026). *On semimonotone matrices of exact order two*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00639>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Here alpha ranges over every finite subset of Fin n, card denotes its cardinality, and A with subscripts alpha alpha is the actual principal submatrix, indexed by the subtype alpha. Every block of size n-k is semimonotone, and every block of every larger size fails semimonotonicity. Sizes are automatically at most n. The condition k at most n is explicit. Fin n relabels the source's indices one through n by zero through n-1.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (IsZMatrix).**
+
+$$(\operatorname{IsZMatrix}\left(A\right)) \Leftrightarrow (\forall (i: \iota), (\forall (j: \iota), ((i \ne j) \Rightarrow (A_{ij} \le 0))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/QuadraticForms/SemimonotoneExactOrderInverseRefutation.IsZMatrix` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bharat Pratap Chauhan; Dipti Dubey (2026). *On semimonotone matrices of exact order two*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00639>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every pair of distinct indices the corresponding entry is nonpositive, exactly the Z-matrix definition in Section 2. Diagonal entries are unrestricted.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (claim).**
+
+$$(claim) \Leftrightarrow (\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\forall (k: \mathbb{N}), (\forall (A: \operatorname{Matrix}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right), \mathbb{R}\right)), ((3 \le n) \Rightarrow ((1 \le k) \Rightarrow ((k < n) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{IsExactOrder}\left(n, k, A\right)) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{det}\left(A\right) < 0) \land ((\operatorname{IsUnit}\left(A\right)) \land (\operatorname{IsZMatrix}\left(A^{-1}\right)))))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/QuadraticForms/SemimonotoneExactOrderInverseRefutation.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Bharat Pratap Chauhan; Dipti Dubey (2026). *On semimonotone matrices of exact order two*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00639>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The assertion quantifies over every natural n and k and every real n by n matrix. Its hypotheses are n at least three, one at most k, k less than n and membership in E_{0_k}. Its conclusion contains all three source requirements: negative determinant, actual invertibility, and a Z-matrix inverse. IsUnit A means that A is a unit in the matrix ring, equivalently it has a two-sided matrix inverse. Although Mathlib's inverse operation is total, IsUnit A is a separate conjunct, so the assertion does not interpret a singular matrix's total inverse as an existing inverse. There is no symmetry, Z-matrix or nonsingularity hypothesis on A.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (counterexample).**
+
+$$counterexample = \operatorname{ofRows}\left(\operatorname{row}\left(1, -5, -2, -2\right), \operatorname{row}\left(-5, 1, -2, -2\right), \operatorname{row}\left(-2, -2, 1, -5\right), \operatorname{row}\left(-2, -2, -5, 1\right)\right)$$

+# A quantitative detector-rank horizon
+
+## Abstract
+
+Short-time density observations bound the spectral tail of an effect under an arbitrary complex subunital completely positive map.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (The universal bound from the original matrices).**
+
+$$\forall D \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall r \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall T \in \operatorname{CompletelyPositiveMap}\left(\operatorname{ComplexEuclideanMatrix}\left(D\right), \operatorname{ComplexEuclideanMatrix}\left(D\right)\right),\; \forall B \in \operatorname{ComplexEuclideanMatrix}\left(D\right),\; \forall sigma \in \operatorname{ComplexEuclideanMatrix}\left(D\right),\; \forall epsilon \in \mathbb{R},\; \forall p \in \mathbb{R},\; \left(2 \le D \land \left(2 \le r \land \left(r \le D \land \left(1 \le n \land \left(\operatorname{apply}\left(T, 1\right) \le 1 \land \left(0 \le B \land \left(B \le 1 \land \left(0 \le sigma \land \left(\operatorname{trace}\left(sigma\right) = 1 \land \left(0 \le epsilon \land \left(0 < p \land \left(p \le 1 \land \left(\left(\forall k \in \mathbb{N},\; k \le D - r \Rightarrow \operatorname{re}\left(\operatorname{trace}\left(sigma \cdot \operatorname{iterate}\left(T, k, B\right)\right)\right) \le epsilon\right) \land p \le \operatorname{re}\left(\operatorname{trace}\left(sigma \cdot \operatorname{iterate}\left(T, n, B\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right) \Rightarrow \operatorname{eigenvalueszero}\left(B, r - 1\right) \le \frac{8 \cdot D}{p^{2}} \cdot \frac{8 \cdot n \cdot D^{\frac{5}{2}}}{p}^{2 \cdot \left(D - r\right)} \cdot epsilon$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Quantum/QuantumChannels/OriginalDataQuantitativeDetectorRankHorizon.detector_rank_horizon` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The matrices act on complex Euclidean space of dimension D. T is completely positive and T(I) is at most I. B is an effect and sigma is a positive matrix of trace one. The eigenvalues of B are ordered decreasingly, with repetitions and zero eigenvalues retained; eigenvalueszero(B,r-1) denotes the r-th eigenvalue. Iteration at zero is the identity. All matrix norms below are Euclidean operator norms.
+
+Put s=lambda_r(B). Nonnegativity settles s=0. For s>0 set t=p s/4, delta=p/(8 n D sqrt(D)), and C=(D/delta)^(D-r). Since s is at most one, t is positive and at most p/4. The threshold delta is positive and less than one. Start with every eigenvector whose eigenvalue is at least t. These vectors form an orthonormal seed of size q at least r. For each seed vector eta, t times its rank-one projection is at most B. Every larger subspace W containing this seed satisfies B at most P_W+t I: on the selected eigenspaces B is at most I, and on the complement every eigenvalue is below t. This construction does not require a spectral gap.
+
+Take the finite Kraus representation of the actual map T, indexed by D squared operators, allowing zero operators. Subunitality makes each Kraus operator a contraction. Apply quantitative_word_orthonormal_extension to this family and the chosen seed. It supplies an orthonormal family e of size m at most D, its projection P, residuals norm((I-P) A_a e_j) at most delta, and expansions of e_j in chronological Kraus words of length at most D-r. The sum of absolute coefficients in each expansion is at most C.
+
+Positivity of individual summands in the same Kraus representation gives t times the rank-one projection onto A_w eta at most T^k(B), where k is the length of w. Trace against sigma and use the early inequalities. The identity Tr(sigma |v><v|)=norm(sqrt(sigma) v) squared yields norm(sqrt(sigma) A_w eta) at most sqrt(epsilon/t). The finite expansions and the triangle inequality then give norm(sqrt(sigma) e_j) at most C sqrt(epsilon/t). Summing over the orthonormal family proves Tr(sigma P) at most D C squared epsilon/t.
+
+Let Q=I-P. Decompose P into its orthonormal rank-one projections and apply the same Kraus representation. Then Q T(P) Q is the sum, over a and j, of rank-one operators on Q A_a e_j. The operator norm of each is at most delta squared. There are at most D cubed terms, so norm(Q T(P) Q) is at most D cubed delta squared. Its square root alpha is therefore at most p/(8 n). This controls the full complex operator, including all off-diagonal coherences.
+
+The spectral cutoff gives X=B-t I at most P. Apply coherent_compression_trace_transfer to T, this P, X and sigma. It gives Re Tr(sigma T^n(X)) at most Tr(sigma P)+2 n alpha. Subunitality implies T^n(I) at most I. Linearity thus gives Re Tr(sigma T^n(B)) at most Tr(sigma P)+2 n alpha+t. The late hypothesis implies p at most D C squared epsilon/t+p/4+p/4. Multiplication by the positive t and substitution t=p s/4 give s at most 8 D C squared epsilon/p squared. Finally D/delta=8 n D^(5/2)/p, giving the displayed constant.
+
+The argument never divides by epsilon and includes epsilon=0. It also includes repeated eigenvalues, singular mixed densities, arbitrary complex coherences, and a late index lying in the early window. No commutation, diagonalizability, conditioning or single-Kraus condition is used. The stronger late-free smallest-eigenvalue endpoint is a separate statement.

+/-- Holomorphic continuation along a real ray forces the defining positive

+    (hpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ x) {a : ℝ} {U : Set ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U)

+    (hinit : (integrableExpSet id μ).Nonempty)
+    (heq : ∀ t : ℝ, t < a → t ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id μ) →
+      F =ᶠ[𝓝 (t : ℂ)] complexMGF id μ) :
+    ∀ t : ℝ, t < a → Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (t * x)) μ := by
+  have hdown {u v : ℝ} (hv : v ∈ integrableExpSet id μ) (huv : u ≤ v) :
+      u ∈ integrableExpSet id μ := by
+    apply hv.mono' (by fun_prop)
+    filter_upwards [hpos] with x hx
+    simp only [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.abs_exp]
+    exact Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right huv hx)
+  intro u hua
+  by_contra hu
+  have hupper (v : ℝ) (hv : v ∈ integrableExpSet id μ) : v ≤ u := by
+    by_contra hvu
+    exact hu (hdown hv (le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge hvu)))
+  have hb : BddAbove (integrableExpSet id μ) := ⟨u, hupper⟩
+  let c : ℝ := sSup (integrableExpSet id μ)
+  have hcu : c ≤ u := csSup_le hinit hupper
+  have hca : c < a := hcu.trans_lt hua
+  have hconv {t : ℝ} (ht : t < c) : t ∈ integrableExpSet id μ := by
+    obtain ⟨v, hv, htv⟩ := exists_lt_of_lt_csSup hinit ht
+    exact hdown hv htv.le
+  obtain ⟨r, hr, hballU⟩ := Metric.isOpen_iff.mp hU (c : ℂ) (hreal c hca)
+  let t : ℝ := c - r / 4
+  have htc : t < c := by dsimp [t]; linarith
+  have ht_int : t ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id μ) := by
+    apply mem_interior.mpr
+    exact ⟨Iio c, fun v hv => hconv hv, isOpen_Iio, htc⟩
+  have hball : Metric.ball (t : ℂ) (r / 2) ⊆ U := by
+    intro z hz
+    apply hballU
+    have hdist : dist (t : ℂ) (c : ℂ) = r / 4 := by
+      rw [dist_eq_norm, ← Complex.ofReal_sub, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs]
+      dsimp [t]
+      rw [show c - r / 4 - c = -(r / 4) by ring, abs_neg, abs_of_pos (by positivity)]
+    have h := dist_triangle z (t : ℂ) (c : ℂ)
+    rw [hdist] at h
+    have hz' : dist z (t : ℂ) < r / 2 := hz
+    change dist z (c : ℂ) < r
+    linarith
+  have hi := integrable_exp_of_holomorphic_extension hpos ht_int (hF.mono hball)
+    (heq t (htc.trans hca) ht_int) (h := r / 3) (by positivity) (by linarith : r / 3 < r / 2)
+  have hle : t + r / 3 ≤ c := le_csSup hb hi
+  dsimp [t] at hle
+  linarith
+
+/-- A positive measure supported on the nonnegative real axis has no
+holomorphic continuation across a finite right endpoint of exponential
+integrability. -/
+theorem nonnegative_exponential_boundary {μ : Measure ℝ}
+    (hpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ x) (c : ℝ)
+    (hconv : ∀ t : ℝ, t < c → Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (t * x)) μ)
+    (hdiv : ∀ t : ℝ, c < t → ¬ Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (t * x)) μ) :
+    ¬ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∃ F : ℂ → ℂ,
+      DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Metric.ball (c : ℂ) r) ∧
+      ∀ z ∈ Metric.ball (c : ℂ) r, z.re < c → F z = complexMGF id μ z := by
+  rintro ⟨r, hr, F, hF, heq⟩
+  let t : ℝ := c - r / 4
+  have ht : t < c := by dsimp [t]; linarith
+  have ht_int : t ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id μ) := by
+    apply mem_interior.mpr
+    refine ⟨Iio c, ?_, isOpen_Iio, ht⟩
+    intro u hu
+    exact hconv u hu
+  have hball : Metric.ball (t : ℂ) (r / 2) ⊆ Metric.ball (c : ℂ) r := by
+    intro z hz
+    have hdist : dist (t : ℂ) (c : ℂ) = r / 4 := by
+      rw [dist_eq_norm, ← Complex.ofReal_sub, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs]
+      dsimp [t]
+      rw [show c - r / 4 - c = -(r / 4) by ring, abs_neg, abs_of_pos (by positivity)]
+    have h := dist_triangle z (t : ℂ) (c : ℂ)
+    rw [hdist] at h
+    have hz' : dist z (t : ℂ) < r / 2 := hz
+    change dist z (c : ℂ) < r
+    linarith
+  have hEq : F =ᶠ[𝓝 (t : ℂ)] complexMGF id μ := by
+    have htc : (t : ℂ) ∈ Metric.ball (c : ℂ) r :=
+      hball (Metric.mem_ball_self (by positivity))
+    filter_upwards [(Metric.isOpen_ball.mem_nhds htc),
+      (isOpen_lt Complex.continuous_re continuous_const).mem_nhds
+        (show (t : ℂ).re < c by simpa using ht)] with z hz hzc
+    exact heq z hz hzc
+  have hi := integrable_exp_of_holomorphic_extension hpos ht_int (hF.mono hball)
+    hEq (h := r / 3) (by positivity) (by linarith : r / 3 < r / 2)
+  exact hdiv (t + r / 3) (by dsimp [t]; linarith) hi
+
+#print axioms integrable_exp_on_real_ray
+#print axioms nonnegative_exponential_boundary
+
+end

+  have hRlim : Tendsto (fun s : ℂ => (s - (rho - 1 / 2)) * R s)
+      (𝓝[≠] (rho - 1 / 2)) (𝓝 0) := by
+    exact vanishing_factor hRc
+  have hPlim : Tendsto (fun s : ℂ => (s - (rho - 1 / 2)) *
+      ((k : ℂ) * (x0 : ℂ) ^ (-s) / s))
+      (𝓝[≠] (rho - 1 / 2)) (𝓝 0) := by
+    exact vanishing_factor hPc
+  refine ⟨m, hm, ?_⟩
+  convert ((hlim.const_mul (e : ℂ)).add hRlim).add hPlim using 1
+  · ext s
+    ring
+  · congr 1 <;> ring
+
+/-- A positive nontrivial zero cannot lie inside the convergence half-plane
+forced by positivity and real-axis regularity. -/
+theorem no_positive_pole {μ : Measure ℝ} (hpos : ∀ᵐ y ∂μ, 0 ≤ y)
+    {a B e k x0 : ℝ} (hx0 : 1 < x0) (he : |e| = 1) {R : ℂ → ℂ}
+    (hR : DifferentiableOn ℂ R {s : ℂ | a < s.re})
+    (hc : ∀ σ : ℝ, B < σ → Integrable (fun y : ℝ => Real.exp (-σ * y)) μ)
+    (hi : ∀ s : ℂ, max B (max a (1 / 2)) < s.re →
+      complexMGF id μ (-s) = (e : ℂ) * regularizedPrincipal s + R s +
+        (k : ℂ) * (x0 : ℂ) ^ (-s) / s)
+    {rho : ℂ} (hρ : IsNontrivialZero rho) :
+    rho.re - 1 / 2 ≤ max a 0 := by
+  by_contra hn
+  have hρgt : max a 0 < (rho - 1 / 2).re := by
+    simpa using lt_of_not_ge hn
+  have hρa : a < (rho - 1 / 2).re := (le_max_left _ _).trans_lt hρgt
+  have hρ0 : rho - (1 / 2 : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
+    intro hz
+    have hzre := congrArg Complex.re hz
+    have : (0 : ℝ) < (rho - 1 / 2).re := (le_max_right _ _).trans_lt hρgt
+    rw [hz] at this
+    norm_num at this
+  have hconv := laplace_integrable hpos hx0 hR hc hi
+  have hsi : (-(rho - (1 / 2 : ℂ))).re ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id μ) :=
+    far_left_interior hconv (by simpa using neg_lt_neg hρgt)
+  have hLc : ContinuousAt (fun s : ℂ => complexMGF id μ (-s)) (rho - 1 / 2) :=
+    ((analyticAt_complexMGF hsi).comp
+      (show AnalyticAt ℂ (fun w : ℂ => -w) (rho - 1 / 2) by fun_prop)).continuousAt
+  have hzero : Tendsto (fun s : ℂ =>
+      (s - (rho - 1 / 2)) * complexMGF id μ (-s))
+      (𝓝[≠] (rho - 1 / 2)) (𝓝 0) := by
+    exact vanishing_factor hLc
+  obtain ⟨m, hm, hres⟩ := continuation_residue hx0 hR hρ hρa hρ0
+  have hevent : ∀ᶠ s : ℂ in 𝓝[≠] (rho - 1 / 2),
+      complexMGF id μ (-s) = (e : ℂ) * regularizedPrincipal s + R s +
+        (k : ℂ) * (x0 : ℂ) ^ (-s) / s := by
+    have hgt : ∀ᶠ s : ℂ in 𝓝 (rho - 1 / 2), max a 0 < s.re :=
+      (isOpen_lt continuous_const Complex.continuous_re).mem_nhds hρgt
+    filter_upwards [normalized_zeta_eventually_ne_zero hρ,
+      Filter.Eventually.filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds hgt] with s hZ hs
+    have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by intro hz; have := (le_max_right a (0 : ℝ)).trans_lt hs; simpa [hz] using this
+    exact identity_on_convergence hx0 hR hc hi ((le_max_left _ _).trans_lt hs)
+      (far_left_interior hconv (by simpa using neg_lt_neg hs)) hs0 hZ
+  have hnonzero : -(e : ℂ) * m / 2 ≠ 0 := by
+    have he0 : e ≠ 0 := by intro hz; simp [hz] at he
+    exact div_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero (neg_ne_zero.mpr (Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr he0))
+      (Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr hm.ne')) two_ne_zero
+  apply hnonzero
+  exact (tendsto_nhds_unique (hzero.congr' (hevent.mono fun s hs => by rw [hs])) hres).symm
+
+/-- A pole on the imaginary axis forces a one-sided budget of at least one half. -/
+theorem critical_pole_budget {μ : Measure ℝ} (hpos : ∀ᵐ y ∂μ, 0 ≤ y)
+    {a B e k x0 : ℝ} (hx0 : 1 < x0) (he : |e| = 1) {R : ℂ → ℂ}
+    (hR : DifferentiableOn ℂ R {s : ℂ | a < s.re})
+    (hc : ∀ σ : ℝ, B < σ → Integrable (fun y : ℝ => Real.exp (-σ * y)) μ)
+    (hi : ∀ s : ℂ, max B (max a (1 / 2)) < s.re →
+      complexMGF id μ (-s) = (e : ℂ) * regularizedPrincipal s + R s +
+        (k : ℂ) * (x0 : ℂ) ^ (-s) / s)
+    (ha : a < 0) {rho : ℂ} (hρ : IsNontrivialZero rho) (hcrit : rho.re = 1 / 2) :
+    (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ k := by
+  let z0 : ℂ := rho - 1 / 2
+  have hzre : z0.re = 0 := by dsimp [z0]; simp [Complex.sub_re, hcrit]
+  have hz0 : z0 ≠ 0 := by
+    intro heq
+    have hρhalf : rho = (1 / 2 : ℂ) := by dsimp [z0] at heq; linear_combination heq
+    have hne := D5.S3.Weil.ZetaBridge.AlternatingZetaContinuation.riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_real_mem_Ioo
+      (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
+    apply hne
+    simpa [hρhalf, D5.S3.Weil.Convention.classicalZeta] using hρ.1
+  have hconv := laplace_integrable hpos hx0 hR hc hi
+  have hzero : max a 0 = 0 := max_eq_right ha.le
+  have hpath : Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ => (σ : ℂ) + z0) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝[≠] z0) := by
+    apply tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff.mpr
+    constructor
+    · simpa using ((Complex.continuous_ofReal.tendsto 0).add_const z0).mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds
+    · filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with σ hσ
+      change (σ : ℂ) + z0 ≠ z0
+      intro heq
+      have : (σ : ℂ) = 0 := add_right_cancel (heq.trans (zero_add z0).symm)
+      exact (ne_of_gt hσ) (Complex.ofReal_eq_zero.mp this)
+  obtain ⟨m, hm, hpole⟩ := continuation_residue hx0 hR hρ (by change a < z0.re; rw [hzre]; exact ha) hz0
+  have hactual : Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ => (σ : ℂ) * complexMGF id μ (-((σ : ℂ) + z0)))
+      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (-(e : ℂ) * m / 2)) := by
+    apply (hpole.comp hpath).congr'
+    have hne0 : ∀ᶠ s : ℂ in 𝓝 z0, s ≠ 0 := compl_singleton_mem_nhds hz0
+    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin,
+      hpath.eventually (normalized_zeta_eventually_ne_zero hρ),
+      hpath.eventually (Filter.Eventually.filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds hne0)]
+      with σ hσ hZ hs0
+    have hsre : max a 0 < ((σ : ℂ) + z0).re := by simpa [hzero, hzre] using hσ
+    have heq := identity_on_convergence hx0 hR hc hi
+      ((le_max_left _ _).trans_lt hsre)
+      (far_left_interior hconv (by simpa using neg_lt_neg hsre)) hs0 hZ
+    dsimp [z0] at *
+    rw [heq]
+    congr 1
+    ring
+  have hRc : ContinuousAt R (0 : ℂ) :=
+    (hR.differentiableAt
+      ((isOpen_lt continuous_const Complex.continuous_re).mem_nhds (by simpa using ha))).continuousAt
+  have hPc : ContinuousAt regularizedPrincipal (0 : ℂ) :=
+    (regularizedPrincipal_analyticAt_real (σ := 0) le_rfl).continuousAt
+  have hx : (x0 : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr (by linarith)
+  have hJ : ContinuousAt (fun s : ℂ => s * ((e : ℂ) * regularizedPrincipal s + R s) +
+      (k : ℂ) * (x0 : ℂ) ^ (-s)) 0 := by fun_prop (disch := assumption)
+  have hmass : Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ => (σ : ℂ) * complexMGF id μ (-(σ : ℂ)))
+      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (k : ℂ)) := by
+    have hlim := (hJ.tendsto.comp (Complex.continuous_ofReal.tendsto 0)).mono_left
+      (nhdsWithin_le_nhds : 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) ≤ 𝓝 (0 : ℝ))
+    simp only [zero_mul, Complex.cpow_zero, neg_zero, mul_one, zero_add] at hlim
+    apply hlim.congr'
+    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with σ hσ
+    have hs : max a 0 < σ := by simpa [hzero] using hσ
+    have hs0 : (σ : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr (ne_of_gt hσ)
+    have hZ : riemannZeta₁ ((σ : ℂ) + 1 / 2) ≠ 0 := by
+      simpa using normalized_zeta_ne_zero_real (x := σ + 1 / 2) (by linarith)
+    rw [identity_on_convergence hx0 hR hc hi
+      ((le_max_left _ _).trans_lt hs) (far_left_interior hconv (by simpa using neg_lt_neg hs)) hs0 hZ]
+    dsimp only [Function.comp_def]
+    field_simp [hs0]
+    <;> ring
+  have hle : ∀ᶠ σ : ℝ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ),
+      ‖(σ : ℂ) * complexMGF id μ (-((σ : ℂ) + z0))‖ ≤
+        ((σ : ℂ) * complexMGF id μ (-(σ : ℂ))).re := by
+    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with σ hσ
+    have hbound := norm_complexMGF_le_mgf (X := id) (μ := μ) (z := -((σ : ℂ) + z0))
+    simp only [Complex.neg_re, Complex.add_re, Complex.ofReal_re, hzre, add_zero] at hbound
+    have hr : (complexMGF id μ (-(σ : ℂ))).re = mgf id μ (-σ) := by
+      rw [← Complex.ofReal_neg, re_complexMGF_ofReal]
+    rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hσ,
+      Complex.mul_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, zero_mul, sub_zero, hr]
+    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hbound hσ.le
+  have hlimit := le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto hactual.norm
+    ((Complex.continuous_re.tendsto _).comp hmass) hle
+  have hn : ‖-(e : ℂ) * m / 2‖ = (m : ℝ) / 2 := by
+    rw [norm_div, norm_mul, norm_neg, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, he]
+    simp
+  rw [hn, Complex.ofReal_re] at hlimit
+  have hm1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ m := by exact_mod_cast (Nat.succ_le_of_lt hm)
+  linarith
+
+#print axioms laplace_integrable
+#print axioms no_positive_pole
+#print axioms critical_pole_budget
+
+end
+end D5.S3.Analytic.Zeta.PositiveLaplacePoleObstruction
