+
+# Acosta Babb's weighted Bessel-kernel positivity conjecture
+
+## Problem
+
+Ryan L. Acosta Babb, *A partial converse to the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma for Bessel–Fourier series of order zero*, arXiv:2410.17681v1, Section 4, Conjecture 1, states:
+
+> For all, $0\leq\alpha\leq\frac12$, $M\in\mathbb N$ and $x\in[0,1]$, $K_M^\alpha(x)\geq0$.
+
+The selected definition is the source's explicit weighted display
+
+$$
+K_M^\alpha(x)=\sum_{m=1}^M\left(1-\frac{m}{M+1}\right)j_m^\alpha J_0(j_mx)\quad(M>0),
+\qquad K_0^\alpha(x)=1.
+$$
+
+Here $j_m$ is the $m$th positive zero of $J_0$. The printed partial sum is $S_m^\alpha(x)=\sum_{k=1}^m j_m^\alpha J_0(j_kx)$. Its factor has index $m$, so the printed Cesàro equality does not follow. The explicit weighted display, rather than that equality, is the target fixed by [#22175](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/22175).
+
+### Statement echo
+
+| Source clause or convention | Lean counterpart | Fidelity |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Standard real $J_0$ | Existing `BesselRedheffer.Defs.nbessel 0` | Reused directly; no new Bessel definition. |
+| Positive zeros indexed from one | `j 1 = firstZero 0`; later `j` are infima of positive zeros strictly above the preceding entry | Literal binding recursive convention; first two infima identified with actual zeros in the proof of `root_brackets`. Index zero is unused. |
+| Printed $S_m^\alpha$ | `S` | The printed index $m$ in the weight is preserved; this definition is separate from `K`. |
+| Weighted formula and exceptional $M=0$ | `K` | Natural indices $1$ through $M$, real weights and real powers; zero branch equals one. |
+| Every real $0\leq\alpha\leq1/2$ | First quantifier and two hypotheses of `claim` | Both endpoints included. |
+| Every natural $M$ and real $0\leq x\leq1$ | Remaining quantifiers and hypotheses of `claim` | Includes zero modes and both interval endpoints. |
+| $K_M^\alpha(x)\geq0$ | Conclusion of `claim` | No extra hypothesis. |
+| Refutation | `result : Not claim` | Exact negation; witness $(\alpha,M,x)=(1/2,2,999/1000)$. |
+
+## Motivation
+
+The conjecture supplies a proposed positivity premise for a stronger Bessel–Fourier coefficient construction. A negative value at two modes decides that premise without a classification for arbitrary mode counts. The source, binding conventions, Tier 1 assessment and partial literature screen are preregistered in #22175. The corresponding source note is [acostababb2024partial](../Library/Estimation/acostababb2024partial.md).
+
+## Gap
+
+No settlement was found in the successful literature screen recorded in #22175. The journal version, *On the rate of growth of Bessel–Fourier coefficients for integrable functions*, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 559 (2026), 130440, DOI 10.1016/j.jmaa.2026.130440, retains Conjecture 1 on p. 11. The unambiguous order-zero arXiv v1 assertion is the formal target. Literature completeness is `ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED`.
+
+**Independent later settlement.** PrincipiaMathOrg/math-solutions independently settles this question in [`site-backup/mathdb-365454/mathdb-365454-solution.tex`](https://github.com/PrincipiaMathOrg/math-solutions/blob/47371706c400c79d06e3fb62190fcf6f7a725c85/site-backup/mathdb-365454/mathdb-365454-solution.tex), at commit `47371706c400c79d06e3fb62190fcf6f7a725c85` (`47371706`), whose first public appearance was 2026-10-27. MJ Kang's solution to [MathDB problem 365454](https://mathdb.com/p/365454/nonnegativity-conjecture-for-the-truncated-bessel-kernel) was posted 2026-10-28. Both public appearances followed preregistration [#22175](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/22175), filed 2026-10-26T07:13:12Z. The open-problem-resolution admission precondition is checked at preregistration; these later public settlements do not invalidate that eligibility or the Lean refutation.
+
+## Route
+
+All declaration names below belong to `D5.S3.Analytic.BesselRedheffer.AcostaBabbKernelRefutation` unless an owner is explicitly named. The existing normalized real Bessel series, coefficient, convergence and derivative facts supply the analytic inputs. Alternating-series remainder bounds enclose the function by finite rational polynomials. Derivative signs, the intermediate value theorem and a negative polynomial certificate between the two root intervals identify the first two positive zeros. The private `two_mode` identity then reduces the weighted sum to two terms, and `point_negative` compares them at the exact witness.
+
+The source-specific admission basis is `open-problem-resolution (#22175; Refuted)`. The theorem steps are classified `bind-only`; no independent escape-witness admission is asserted. The public result is the designated refutation result (`basis=refutes`) and is exempt from four-slot escape registration (CLAUDE.md §3.9).
+
+## Falsifier
+
+The source assertion would require $K_2^{1/2}(999/1000)\geq0$. The module proves the strict opposite. A different interpretation based on repairing the printed $S$ formula is outside the bound target. Identifying the first two zeros is proved without adding zero-existence or zero-ordering hypotheses to `claim`.
+
+## Evidence
+
+The settling declaration is `D5.S3.Analytic.BesselRedheffer.AcostaBabbKernelRefutation.result`. Its private proof dependencies include `root_brackets`, `scaled_a_value`, `scaled_b_value` and `point_negative`. The canonical frozen state record is `Golden/Frozen/state/D5/S3/Analytic/BesselRedheffer/AcostaBabbKernelRefutation.lean.json`; the Scribe records one `OpenProblemResolutionClaim` with resolution `Refuted` on `result`.
+
+### Exact rational experiment
+
+[Experiment directory at commit b01beb85ba641ba44f5d5711499d06a46af0ddef](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing-experiments/tree/b01beb85ba641ba44f5d5711499d06a46af0ddef/docs/reports/acosta-babb-bessel-kernel).
+
+Command, from that repository root: `python3 docs/reports/acosta-babb-bessel-kernel/check.py`; exit code 0. Script SHA-256: `ce3c873f27837df0248c09ec4c25d95d6a159658aeaed7ef0457db174a8acef1`.
+
+The script checks forty rational coefficient identities, root-endpoint signs and transferred derivative intervals, integer-power comparisons, and rational margins. It computes $27843/500000$ for the endpoint derivative lower comparison and $895734319/60000000<15$ for the curvature upper comparison. Its power comparisons correspond to $17/50<\alpha_*<7/20$. These finite comparisons do not prove the uniform-family or sharp-threshold analytic bridges. At the single point $(\alpha,M,x)=(1/2,2,999/1000)$, it computes the exact interval
+
+$$
+-\frac{182022699}{10^{12}}\leq K_2^{1/2}(999/1000)\leq-\frac{89362407}{500000000000}<0.
+$$
+
+The interval computation is separate from the Lean proof, which uses the weaker sufficient rational bounds below. No uniform analytic conclusion is attributed to the computation.
+
+## Triage
+
+1. **Proved in the module (kernel-checked):** the explicit weighted positivity conjecture is false at $\alpha=1/2$, $M=2$, $x=999/1000$. Evidence: private `point_negative` and public `result`.
+2. **Proved in the module (kernel-checked):** private `root_brackets` gives
+   $24048255/10^7\leq j_1\leq24048256/10^7$ and $55200781/10^7\leq j_2\leq55200782/10^7$.
+   Its proof identifies the infima with actual zeros. `order_one_positive`, `order_one_negative`, `first_decreasing`, `second_increasing` and `middle_negative` exclude earlier or intervening zeros; the intermediate value theorem supplies the two zeros.
+3. **Proved in the module (kernel-checked):** the private `scaled_a_value` and `scaled_b_value` estimates give $J_0(ax)\leq1/800$ and $J_0(bx)\leq-187/100000$ for the isolated $a=j_1$, $b=j_2$ and $x=999/1000$. The proof of `point_negative` also establishes $\sqrt a\leq1551/1000$ and $\sqrt b\geq2349/1000$, and uses these to make the negative second weighted mode exceed twice the first in magnitude.
+4. **Computed:** the experiment entry above checks the endpoint-flux comparison $27843/500000$, curvature comparison $895734319/60000000$, and integer-power comparisons associated with $17/50<\alpha_*<7/20$. Evidence: the pinned `check.py`, command, exit code and SHA-256 above. The uniform-family and sharp-threshold analytic bridges are not Lean theorems of this delivery.
+5. **Open:** formal sharp $M=2$ sign classification and the uniform $\alpha\in[2/5,1/2]$ endpoint rectangle. The finite experiment checks their rational inputs, not those analytic bridges.
+6. **Open:** positivity in other parameter ranges or for other $M$; the downstream existence assertions in Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.2; and Conjecture 2. Refuting the positivity premise removes the proposed conditional route, not those downstream conclusions themselves.
+
+### What the settlement shows
+
+**Proved in the module:** at the single point the larger negative contribution of the second mode defeats the conjectured nonnegativity. This is the mechanism established by `point_negative`; a uniform endpoint-flux argument is not part of that theorem.
+
+**Explanation by rational arithmetic:** the mode estimates in `point_negative` give the sufficient upper comparison
+
+$$
+\frac{2(1551/1000)(1/800)-(2349/1000)(187/100000)}{3}
+=-\frac{17171}{100000000}<0.
+$$
+
+**Proved in prose from the definition:** the exceptional zero-mode kernel remains $K_0^\alpha(x)=1$, since this is the zero branch of `K`. This surviving statement requires no assertion about other mode counts or exponents. **Literature-attested:** the journal's weaker uniform lower bound in Lemma 3.3 is compatible with a negative interval and is not refuted by the point witness. It is not on this module's dependency path.
+
+**Open:** the sharp transition, the proposed uniform rectangle, and other positivity ranges require further analytic work. Theorem 5.1, Corollary 5.2 and the conditional Proposition 5.3 discussion lose the proposed positivity-based route; their existence conclusions and Conjecture 2 remain undecided here.
+
+## ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED
+
+Literature completeness and originality are unverified. The successful source and citation screen is recorded in #22175; MathOverflow, rate-limited citation queries, unread final journal texts, uncapped broader arXiv results and full classical treatises are outside that screen. The result is repository-derived; no originality claim is made. No sharp sign classification or uniform counterexample family is claimed as kernel-checked.

+
+# The simple evolution-algebra automorphism maximum
+
+## Problem
+
+Kaygorodov, Martín González and Viruel, *Evolution algebras: a survey of
+results and a list of open problems*, arXiv:2610.22248v1, Conjecture 4,
+section 2.3, page 28:
+
+> Over ℂ, the maximal order of the automorphism group of a simple
+> n-dimensional evolution algebra is max{n!, n(2ⁿ−1)}.
+
+The dimension is positive. The source's natural-basis condition is zero
+mixed products. The product is complex bilinear and commutative, without
+associativity or a multiplicative unit. Automorphisms are the entire group
+of complex linear multiplication-preserving equivalences.
+
+### Statement echo
+
+| Source clause | Lean counterpart |
+| --- | --- |
+| Every positive dimension | `claim` quantifies over $n\in\mathbb N$ with $1\le n$ |
+| Every complex vector space of dimension $n$ | Arbitrary carrier, complex module, finite-dimensional instance and finrank equality |
+| Evolution product and natural basis | Bilinear product, arbitrary finite basis, zero mixed products and commutativity |
+| Simple algebra | `IsSimple`: $A^2\ne0$ and every complex-linear two-sided ideal is zero or the whole space |
+| Full finite automorphism group and upper bound | `Finite (Aut μ)` together with the bound on `Nat.card` |
+| Maximum is attained | A product on $\mathbb C^n$ with the dimension, commutativity, natural basis, simplicity, finiteness and exact cardinality |
+
+The simplicity definition is literal: “We recall that an algebra A is
+simple if A² ≠ 0 and 0 is the only proper ideal.” This sentence is from
+the survey's cited arXiv:1601.01832v2, section 4, page 18. All two-sided
+complex-linear ideals are quantified, including those not spanned by
+natural-basis vectors. The coordinate representative in the attainment
+clause does not restrict the universal clause. `Finite` prevents the
+natural cardinality of an infinite group from satisfying a bound through
+its value zero. The extra dimension equality in the attaining clause
+records that the chosen representative has the required dimension.
+
+## Motivation
+
+The full group has a diagonal kernel and a permutation image constrained
+by the same support graph. Simplicity adds strong connectivity to the
+invertible structure map. The target is their joint maximum, rather than
+the product of separately achievable maxima. Preregistration: #21769.
+
+## Gap
+
+The survey reports small-dimensional verification and two attaining
+families. Those assertions alone do not give the uniform upper bound.
+The needed structural step is that strong connectivity makes the least
+successor-compatible quotient one cycle, and an actual supported
+permutation gives all of its fibers the same positive cardinality.
+
+## Route
+
+In the settling module, `simple_perfect` and `simple_support_connected`
+derive perfection and strong connectivity directly from the ideal
+condition. `connected_beta_cycle` projects paths to successor orbits.
+`supported_permutation` extracts a nonzero determinant term.
+`equal_fibers` restricts that permutation to consecutive quotient fibers,
+so their common size $k$ and the quotient size $h$ satisfy $n=hk$.
+The existing `EvolutionAutomorphismControl.automorphism_quotient_bound`
+then bounds the actual full group by $h(2^h-1)(k!)^h$.
+`factorial_period_bound` bounds this by $(hk)!$ when $h,k\ge2$;
+the boundary cases $h=1$ and $k=1$ give the two required alternatives.
+`simple_bound` transports the estimate to the arbitrary carrier and basis.
+
+`cyclic_family` proves simplicity and exact full-group order
+$n(2^n-1)$ for the cyclic product. `complete_simple` and
+`complete_aut_card` give the corresponding facts with order $n!$ for the
+product of structure matrix $I+J$. Every coordinate permutation lifts;
+loops force the diagonal kernel to be trivial. `result` chooses the
+larger family in each dimension.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+A positive-dimensional simple complex evolution algebra with an infinite
+full automorphism group, or order above the asserted maximum, would
+contradict the universal clause. Failure of either attaining product to
+have the required simplicity or exact full-group order would invalidate
+attainment. A statement about a coordinate subgroup would not settle
+this question about the full group.
+
+## Evidence
+
+The settling declaration is
+`D5/S3/QuadraticForms/EvolutionAlgebras/SimpleEvolutionAutomorphismMaximum.result`.
+It proves the literal `claim` with both universal bound and attainment.
+The conjecture source note is `Library/QuadraticForms/kaygorodov2026evolution.md`; the simplicity definition is recorded in `Library/QuadraticForms/cabrera2016evolution.md`.
+
+The four-slot escape audit is unfinished for `result` and the seven
+published owner declarations named in
+[issue #22095](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/22095).
+No completed escape registration is claimed.
+
+### Exact experiment
+
+The experiment is in
+[trureturing-experiments at 638f7495de97c6d37ce040add1ab2d8ab6329195](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing-experiments/tree/638f7495de97c6d37ce040add1ab2d8ab6329195/docs/reports/kmv-c4-simpleaut).
+The pinned `check.py` has SHA-256
+`e2bde776354a34d528a36e2c19ef073fd45b90b23ca82c86403d74d188654389`.
+Command executed on its exact extracted bytes:
+`python3 /tmp/op-kmvc4/doors/check.py`,
+exit 0. It uses exact integers and rational numbers.
+
+## Triage
+
+### What the settlement shows
+
+1. **Proved in the module:** `result` gives the exact maximum in every
+   positive dimension. **Proved in prose from that formula:** in dimension
+   four it is $\max\{24,60\}=60$, and in dimension six it is
+   $\max\{720,378\}=720$. The previously available all-perfect-algebra
+   envelope has values $72$ and $1296$ in these dimensions, as stated by
+   `EvolutionAutomorphismMaximum.result`; that comparison theorem is not
+   on this module's dependency path. The simple restriction therefore
+   sharpens those values to $60$ and $720$.
+2. **Proved in the module:** `connected_beta_cycle`, `supported_permutation`
+   and `equal_fibers` establish the joint mechanism for the same algebra.
+   `coordinate_simple_bound` uses the resulting single quotient cycle and
+   common fiber size in the actual kernel/image estimate. Separate
+   optima of the two group factors are not combined as if jointly attained.
+3. **Proved in the module:** `cyclic_family`, `complete_simple` and
+   `complete_aut_card` establish simplicity and full-group orders
+   $n(2^n-1)$ and $n!$ of the cyclic and $I+J$ families for all positive $n$.
+4. **Proved in the module:** `simple_bound` needs the finite natural-basis
+   zero-mixed-product law, simplicity and the dimension, with no separate
+   commutativity hypothesis. The public claim retains the source's

+
+# Sun Conjecture 4.2(i) absolute-difference permanent congruences
+
+## Problem
+
+Zhi-Wei Sun, *Arithmetic properties of some permanents*, arXiv:2108.07723v7,
+Conjecture 4.2(i), equations (4.3) and (4.4), asks whether for every odd prime
+$p$ the permanents of the matrices with entries $|j-k|$ and $|j-k+1|$ are
+congruent to $-1/2$ and $1/2$ modulo $p$, respectively. The integer encoding is
+$A_s(j,k)=|((j.val:\mathbb Z)+1)-((k.val:\mathbb Z)+1)+s|$ for
+$j,k : \operatorname{Fin} p$ and $s=0,1$.
+
+### Statement echo
+
+The source permanent is the finite sum over permutations of products of
+row-indexed entries. The Lean claim clears the invertible denominator 2 and
+states both divisibilities for the same universally quantified odd prime.
+
+## Motivation
+
+The result settles the two explicitly numbered congruences in the source's
+open-conjecture section and gives a uniform prime-order mechanism for both
+absolute-difference shifts.
+
+## Gap
+
+The source left both congruences conjectural. The bounded literature screen in
+issue #22003 found the Brualdi--Newman prime circulant congruence as the classical
+ingredient, but no prior proof of this absolute-difference pair. Literature
+completeness and worldwide priority remain `ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED`.
+
+## Route
+
+For odd prime $p$, alternating row and column signs reduce each absolute-
+difference matrix modulo $p$ to a circulant. Prime-order conjugation of
+permutation weights cancels nonfixed orbits in characteristic $p$; the fixed
+permutations are translations. Fermat's identity evaluates their weights, and
+the alternating sum over $0,\ldots,2m$ with $p=2m+1$ is $m+s$. Clearing the
+factor 2 gives the two integer divisibilities.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+The settled claim is
+\[
+\forall p\in\mathbb N,\;p\text{ prime}\to p\text{ odd}\to
+((p:\mathbb Z)\mid 2\operatorname{per}(A_0)+1)\land
+((p:\mathbb Z)\mid 2\operatorname{per}(A_1)-1).
+\]
+Its falsifier would be an odd prime and one failed divisibility.
+
+## Evidence
+
+The kernel-checked declaration is
+`D5/S3/Combinatorics/Permanental/SunAbsoluteDifferenceCongruences.result`.
+The escape audit for this public theorem is unfinished and is tracked in
+https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/22464.
+The finite checks are in the [pinned experiment directory](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing-experiments/tree/8478b9fc028dfcf192a82eff0aa7b6b25fe0a111/docs/reports/sun-2108-conj42i-permanents).
+The script is `docs/reports/sun-2108-conj42i-permanents/check.py`, SHA-256
+`a549c0f6573ad0e1452dbe7719d51f6d6f7ed11d83e48917650986aed9cc4678`.
+Command `python3 -u /tmp/op-sun210842/experiment-rework/check.py`, run on
+the exact script bytes extracted from that commit, exits 0
+and reports the exact target checks for odd primes $p=3,5,7,11,13,17,19$,
+the sign reduction at every odd prime $p\le101$ for shifts $0,1$, and the prime circulant checks at
+$p=3,5$.
+
+## Triage
+
+| item | status | evidence |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Both Conjecture 4.2(i) divisibilities for every odd prime. | proved | Kernel-checked `SunAbsoluteDifferenceCongruences.result`; the alternating-sign, prime-orbit and telescoping-sum mechanism is the proof route. |
+| For every prime $p$ and $f : \operatorname{ZMod}(p)\to\operatorname{ZMod}(p)$, the permanent of the circulant equals $\sum_a f(a)$, including $p=2$. | proved | The consumed private `permanent_circulant` declaration in the settling proof, using prime-order fixed-point counting. This is the Brualdi--Newman ingredient and is not claimed as new mathematics. |
+| The alternating-sign entry reduction holds at every odd natural order for shifts $s=0,1$. | proved | The consumed private `sign_entry` declaration. |
+| The alternating weighted sum over $0,\ldots,2m$ equals $m+s$ for all $m:\mathbb N$ and $s:\mathbb Z$. | proved | The consumed private `alternating_sum` declaration. |
+| The odd composite extension fails at $n=9$ for both shifts. | proved in prose | The cyclic-orbit reduction below gives the cleared residues $6$ and $3$ modulo $9$. |
+| The same entry identity fails at shift $2$. | proved in prose | Direct substitution below gives residues $2$ and $1$ for $p=3$, $i=0$, $j=1$, $s=2$. |
+| Classification for other shifts, composite moduli and stronger prime-power congruences. | open | No declaration in this delivery settles these neighbouring questions. |
+| Lean formalization of part (ii)'s reciprocal-sum formula. | open | The screened Jiang--Sun paper addresses that distinct formula; no Lean declaration here addresses it. |
+
+
+### Neighbouring assertions proved in prose
+
+The following arguments establish the neighbouring claims without using the
+finite experiment above. They are paper proofs, not additional Lean theorems.
+
+For $s\in\{0,1\}$ put $f_s(u)=(-1)^u(u+s)$ for the representative
+$u\in\{0,\ldots,8\}$, with values in $\mathbb Z/9\mathbb Z$. The odd-order
+entry identity of `sign_entry`, together with `permanent_sign` and
+`permanent_map`, identifies the reduction of $\operatorname{per}(A_s)$ at
+order $9$ with the permanent of the circulant with entries $f_s(x-y)$.
+Those three helpers require no primality assumption.
+
+Let $t(x)=x+1$ on $\mathbb Z/9\mathbb Z$ and conjugate permutations by $t$.
+The weight $w(\sigma)=\prod_x f_s(\sigma(x)-x)$ is constant on each orbit.
+The orbit sizes divide $9$. Orbits of size $9$ contribute zero modulo $9$;
+the union of the other orbits is exactly the set of permutations commuting
+with $t^3$. Hence the circulant permanent equals the sum of $w$ over this set.
+
+Every permutation commuting with $t^3$ has a unique description
+$\sigma(r+3k)=\pi(r)+3(k+a_r)$, with $r,k\in\{0,1,2\}$,
+$\pi\in S_3$, and each $a_r\in\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z$. Conversely every
+such choice is a commuting permutation. Its weight is
+$\prod_r f_s(\pi(r)-r+3a_r)^3$, where arguments are reduced modulo $9$.
+Summing independently over the three $a_r$ reduces the answer to the permanent
+of the $3\times3$ matrix $B_s(r,q)=b_s(q-r)$, where indices are modulo $3$ and
+$b_s(d)=\sum_{a=0}^2 f_s(d+3a)^3$.
+
+The six entries are obtained by the explicit integer sums
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+b_0(0)&=0^3+(-3)^3+6^3\equiv0,&
+b_0(1)&=(-1)^3+4^3+(-7)^3\equiv-1,&
+b_0(2)&=2^3+(-5)^3+8^3\equiv-1,\\
+b_1(0)&=1^3+(-4)^3+7^3\equiv1,&
+b_1(1)&=(-2)^3+5^3+(-8)^3\equiv1,&
+b_1(2)&=3^3+(-6)^3+9^3\equiv0
+\pmod9.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+For $B_0$, only the two $3$-cycles contribute, giving
+$\operatorname{per}(B_0)=2(-1)^3\equiv7\pmod9$.
+For $B_1$, only the identity and one $3$-cycle contribute, each with weight
+$1$, giving $\operatorname{per}(B_1)\equiv2\pmod9$.
+Thus the two cleared expressions are congruent to $2\cdot7+1\equiv6$ and
+$2\cdot2-1\equiv3$ modulo $9$, respectively. Both are nonzero.
+This proves failure of the odd-composite extension at order $9$; it makes no
+claim about other composite orders or exact integer permanent values.
+
+For the shift-$2$ entry identity take $p=3$, $i=0$, $j=1$. Its left side is
+$(-1)^{0+1}|0-1+2|=-1\equiv2\pmod3$.
+The representative of $i-j$ is $2$, so the right side is
+$(-1)^2(2+2)=4\equiv1\pmod3$. The entries are unequal.
+
+### What the settlement shows
+
+**Proved by `result`:** both absolute-difference permanent congruences hold for
+every odd prime. The decisive mechanism is the alternating-sign reduction to a
+prime circulant, cancellation of nonfixed permutation-weight orbits, and the
+fixed-translation evaluation.
+
+**Scope:** the entry reduction is proved for odd natural orders and shifts
+$s=0,1$; the counting step requires primality. The argument does not settle
+other shifts, composite moduli or prime-power strengthening.
+
+**Effect on the source:** Conjecture 4.2(i), including (4.3) and (4.4), is
+settled positively. Part (ii) is a separate assertion addressed by the screened Jiang--Sun paper;
+its Lean formalization is outside this delivery.
+
+## ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED
+
+The literature search is bounded by the sources and services recorded in issue
+#22003. It does not certify exhaustive worldwide priority or completeness.
